title: Lecture 8 Boss Problems
subtitle: Problem solving with decisions: the if statement

parity.starter:
number = int(input('Number: '))
# Print whether the number is even or odd.
parity.check:
import re
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1, "Use exactly one if statement."
assert re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "Handle the other case with else."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "elif is not part of this lecture; one if and one else are enough here."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Choose the value inside the branches, then print once after them."
assert "%" in __code__, "Test the remainder with % to tell even from odd."
assert __stdout__.strip().endswith("."), "End the message with a full stop, as in 14 is even."
parity.answerNote: number % 2 is 0 for every even number, including 0 and negative numbers.

dog.starter:
years = float(input('Human years: '))
# Print the age in dog years to one decimal place.

cases.name: Typed 7
cases.expected: Human years: 7.0 human years is 41.0 dog years.

cases.name: Typed 2
cases.expected: Human years: 2.0 human years is 21.0 dog years.

cases.name: Typed 1
cases.expected: Human years: 1.0 human years is 10.5 dog years.

cases.name: Typed 15
cases.expected: Human years: 15.0 human years is 73.0 dog years.

cases.name: Typed 1.2
cases.expected: Human years: 1.2 human years is 12.6 dog years.

dog.check:
import re
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1, "Use exactly one if statement."
assert re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "Handle the other case with else."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "elif is not part of this lecture; one if and one else are enough here."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Choose the value inside the branches, then print once after them."
assert re.search(r":[^}]*\.1f\}", __source__), "Show both numbers to one decimal place with :.1f in the f-string."
assert "10.5" in __code__ and re.search(r"\b4\b", __code__), "Use 10.5 dog years for each of the first two years and 4 for each year after that."
hints: The decision is whether `years` is 2 or less. If so, the whole age is at the 10.5 rate. Otherwise it is 21 for the first two years plus 4 for each year beyond them: `21 + (years - 2) * 4`.
dog.answerNote: The first two years are worth 21 dog years. The else branch starts from 21 and adds 4 for each remaining year. Both formulas give 21 at exactly 2 years.

square.starter:
position = input('Square: ')
# Print whether the square is black or white.

cases.name: Typed a1
cases.expected: Square: a1 is a black square.

cases.name: Typed d5
cases.expected: Square: d5 is a white square.

cases.name: Typed h1
cases.expected: Square: h1 is a white square.

cases.name: Typed g7
cases.expected: Square: g7 is a black square.

cases.name: Typed c6
cases.expected: Square: c6 is a white square.

square.check:
import re
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1, "Use exactly one if statement."
assert re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "Handle the other case with else."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "elif is not part of this lecture; one if and one else are enough here."
assert __code__.count("print(") == 1, "Choose the value inside the branches, then print once after them."
assert ".find(" in __code__, "Turn the column letter into a number with 'abcdefgh'.find(...) instead of testing each letter."
assert "%" in __code__, "Use % to decide the colour from the column number and the row."
assert "ord(" not in __code__, "ord() is not part of this course; use .find() on the string of column letters."
assert "[" in __code__, "Pick the letter and the digit out of position with indexes."
hints: Add the column number to the row number, `int(position[1])`. Moving one square in any direction changes the sum by one, so the sum is odd on every black square and even on every white one. For `a1` it is 0 + 1.
square.answerNote: 'abcdefgh'.find('a') is 0. For a1 the sum is 0 + 1, which is odd, and a1 is black. Each move of one square changes the sum by one and the colour flips.
